findings.title: Bestehenden MFA-Faktor ohne Step-up ersetzbar
findings.evidence: evidence/adversarial-probes.json: MFA-enabled synthetic session → setup200, confirm200; confirm route19–25 verifies only the new secret.
findings.rootCause: Setup accepts any session; no current factor/password/recent MFA check. Confirm writes current pending secret after an unlocked read.
findings.proposedCorrection: Differentiate first enrollment from factor replacement. Require recent current-factor step-up, lock/CAS the verified pending secret, audit change and invalidate appropriate sessions.
findings.consumers: security-settings-page; MFA setup/confirm; all authenticated users
findings.risk: Compromised active session can replace account second factor. Setup/confirm race may persist a different pending secret. No real takeover executed.
findings.testRequirement: Existing MFA enabled + missing/wrong old factor must fail; first required enrollment still works; parallel setup/confirm proves only the verified secret is promoted.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: Replacement requires valid recent step-up and atomic promotion; old/new secret and recovery hashes never enter logs.
findings.status: Original audit evidence retained; see remediationStatus
findings.proofLimit: Real handler with synthetic DB/crypto stubs. Proves missing control-flow guard, not a production account compromise.
findings.implementation: Existing MFA replacement denied by both handlers. First enrollment verifies a row-locked pending secret, revokes other sessions and writes an audit event in the same transaction.
findings.verification: scripts/auth-integrity-test.mjs; PostgreSQL CI repeat required

findings.title: Recovery-Code wird nicht atomar verbraucht
findings.evidence: evidence/recovery-race.json: two forced concurrent real-handler calls with same synthetic recovery code → [200,200],2 sessions.
findings.rootCause: Login reads recovery hashes in initial user SELECT then overwrites array without row lock or conditional atomic removal.
findings.proposedCorrection: Consume recovery hash in one transaction / conditional UPDATE RETURNING and grant login only if exactly one claim succeeds. Preserve password verification.
findings.consumers: Login; recovery fallback; all MFA accounts
findings.risk: One-time guarantee fails under concurrent valid-password requests; competing distinct-code writes can restore a removed hash.
findings.testRequirement: Real PostgreSQL16 simultaneous same-code and distinct-code logins; assert one same-code session and no lost removals.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: A recovery code yields at most one successful claim; failed transactions leave recoverable consistent state.
findings.status: Original audit evidence retained; see remediationStatus
findings.proofLimit: Synthetic concurrency scheduler reproduces handler logic. Exact production timing and PostgreSQL parallel exploit were not executed locally.
findings.implementation: Atomic conditional removal from the current recovery hash array; same code succeeds once, distinct codes cannot resurrect each other.
findings.verification: scripts/auth-integrity-test.mjs --postgres

findings.title: Passwort-Reset ist nicht atomar
findings.evidence: evidence/adversarial-probes.json: token consumption precedes injected password-update failure; response500.
findings.rootCause: Token consumption, password update and session deletion are separate pool statements.
findings.proposedCorrection: Use one transaction for token claim, password change and session invalidation; hash first with bounded password length.
findings.consumers: auth-tokens; reset form; auth_sessions
findings.risk: Link can be lost before password change; failure after password update can leave old sessions alive. Current-password branch already has transaction.
findings.testRequirement: Inject failure before/after each DB statement and assert rollback; parallel reset replay fails; old sessions revoked on success.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: All three operations commit together or leave prior state; safe retry and bounded password input.
findings.status: Original audit evidence retained; see remediationStatus
findings.implementation: Token consumption, active-user password change and session deletion share one transaction; bounded hashing happens first.
findings.verification: scripts/auth-integrity-test.mjs: injected deletion fault, rollback, retry and consumed-token denial

findings.title: Scanstatus wirkt nicht als Quarantäne
findings.evidence: evidence/file-pwa-probes.json: pending file returns200. Upload writes pending at files/route.ts52–54; no scanner transition found in runtime code.
findings.rootCause: MIME signatures and tenant guards exist, but download/PDF-logo consumers ignore scan_status.
findings.proposedCorrection: Define explicit scanner/quarantine policy centrally; integrate asynchronous scanning and gate all consumers consistently; plan existing pending files safely.
findings.consumers: entity-files; download; documentLogo; attachments
findings.risk: Potential malicious-file propagation; signature check is not a malware scan. No malicious payload used or compromise demonstrated.
findings.testRequirement: pending/rejected/clean downloads and PDF-logo ingestion; scan failure and authorized retry; tenant isolation.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: Only policy-approved content is delivered; rejected/pending behavior documented and enforced without silently blocking all existing files.
findings.status: Original audit evidence retained; see remediationStatus
findings.implementation: Download and PDF-logo quarantine enforced. Central fail-closed local ClamAV INSTREAM integration added; clean-only logo/avatar publication and tenant/purpose-scoped company references protected. Scanner infrastructure, real-engine detection, deployed limits/signatures and legacy pending-file rescan remain unproven.
findings.verification: scripts/file-scan-test.mjs (protocol peer only; OS socket in CI), scripts/auth-integrity-test.mjs and settings browser cases; docs/security/file-scanning.md defines remaining live scanner acceptance. No production release claim.

findings.title: Freitext-Fehler umgehen Redaction
findings.evidence: evidence/adversarial-probes.json: logger redacts email key but preserves synthetic personal marker in detail; email.ts58–59 logs provider response text; http.ts69 prints raw Error.message.
findings.rootCause: Key-based redaction cannot sanitize provider strings or arbitrary exception messages.
findings.proposedCorrection: Use allowlisted error codes/request correlation; redact free text before logging; do not log raw provider payloads.
findings.consumers: logger; http.apiError; Graph token/mail errors
findings.risk: Provider/user details may enter logs; no real secret or personal data reproduced.
findings.testRequirement: Synthetic email/token/IBAN markers in nested objects, provider text and DB errors; assert no markers logged.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: Logs contain safe metadata and correlation IDs only; diagnostics remain sufficient.
findings.status: Original audit evidence retained; see remediationStatus
findings.implementation: Provider free text/recipient/subject removed from mail logs; API errors log category only; logger redacts sensitive payload fields.
findings.verification: scripts/runtime-integrity-test.mjs

findings.title: Origin- und IP-Prüfung setzt vertrauenswürdige Forwarded-Header voraus
findings.evidence: assertSameOrigin permits missing Origin and extends allowlist from request Host/x-forwarded-host; rate-limit.ts8 accepts first forwarded IP.
findings.rootCause: Trusted ingress boundary is implicit; source itself does not authenticate forwarding metadata. SameSite cookies reduce cross-site risk.
findings.proposedCorrection: Verify Azure header stripping/trusted proxy topology; constrain origin allowlist and trusted IP extraction centrally; retain legitimate non-browser webhook flows.
findings.consumers: All assertSameOrigin/enforceRateLimit consumers
findings.risk: Potential bypass only if ingress accepts attacker-controlled forwarding headers. Not a proven CSRF/rate-limit exploit.
findings.testRequirement: Ingress spoofed Host/forwarded headers; Origin absent/null/mismatched; cross-site same-site requests; forged forwarded IP cannot reset bucket.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: Only trusted ingress metadata used; browser mutations follow documented origin policy.
findings.status: Original audit evidence retained; see remediationStatus
findings.implementation: Forwarded host/IP trust depends on Azure ingress configuration. No configuration assumptions or blind auth change made.
findings.verification: Read-only Azure ingress proof and origin/IP-spoof tests still required

findings.title: Body-Limits greifen nach vollständigem Einlesen
findings.evidence: Multipart formData precedes 10MiB per-file check; http.ts15 reads text fully before length verification; webhook same pattern.
findings.rootCause: Application size checks limit persisted data but do not bound bytes read/parsed for missing/false Content-Length or multipart aggregate.
findings.proposedCorrection: Document ingress byte caps and implement bounded streaming/aggregate multipart parsing; per-user/tenant quotas and controlled upload rate.
findings.consumers: Uploads; database bytea storage; webhook; JSON APIs
findings.risk: Memory/DB pressure possible under authenticated large requests; actual memory exhaustion not tested.
findings.testRequirement: Chunked oversized requests, multiple files, forged Content-Length; bounded memory and deterministic413; proxy/application consistency.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: Rejected requests stop within configured total byte budget; tenant storage usage limit enforced or explicit contract.
findings.status: Original audit evidence retained; see remediationStatus
findings.implementation: JSON, multipart uploads and signed Stripe webhook are bounded during stream reads, including chunked bodies.
findings.verification: scripts/runtime-integrity-test.mjs plus actual upload handlers

findings.title: Datei-Erstellung besitzt keine Replay-Identität
findings.evidence: Every POST generates randomUUID and inserts file_objects+file_contents; no Idempotency-Key or dedup lookup in handler.
findings.rootCause: Upload path diverges from central idempotentBusiness contract used by document/project/etc. creates.

findings.title: Veralteter Login kann nach abgeschlossenem Passwort-Reset eine Sitzung anlegen
findings.evidence: Synthetic real-handler/real-session/PGlite barrier probe at 0c7947f: reset commits before login resumes; HTTP200 and one newly persisted session. No production account touched.
findings.rootCause: Credential verification and later session INSERT are not synchronized with password/MFA revocation; authenticated password change writes independently of its previously verified hash.
findings.proposedCorrection: Lock current user state and bind expected password/MFA snapshot to session INSERT in one transaction; CAS authenticated password changes against the verified hash.
findings.consumers: Login, password reset/change, shared createSession; email verification keeps its own token proof with an active-user check.
findings.risk: An in-flight stale authentication can survive session revocation; an in-flight authenticated password change can overwrite a reset. Requires the earlier credential proof; no real account compromise executed.
findings.testRequirement: Deterministic read barriers, real session INSERT, reset-first/old-login denial, fresh login, stale password change, changed MFA and inactive status; repeat with physical PostgreSQL clients.
findings.acceptanceCriterion: Reset-first stale login returns401 with zero persisted sessions; stale password change returns409 and preserves reset hash; valid current proofs still work.
findings.status: Reproduced on frozen draft; central correction implemented; see verification and release blockers
findings.proofLimit: Actual handlers, actual session owner, synthetic cookie/header adapters and isolated database. Deployed runtime not verified.
findings.implementation: User-row-locked credential-bound session INSERT; all callers reject inactive users. Login supplies verified password/MFA snapshot. Authenticated password change uses hash/status CAS. No schema migration.
findings.verification: scripts/auth-integrity-test.mjs using actual session owner; native PostgreSQL CI and final head checks required. docs/security/auth-state-integrity.md
